newsitem.title: USA: Muni traders see no panic selling of Miami bonds.
newsitem.headline: Muni traders see no panic selling of Miami bonds.

text.p: Despite Miami's fiscal crisis and its bond rating downgrades to non-investment level, bond traders said Tuesday there had been no panic selling of Miami bonds, which are mostly insured.
"We havn't seen a one," one Florida municipal bond trader said.
Another trader concurred, saying, "I haven't seen any to be honest with you, maybe a couple of odd lots. They're going to trade off some, but I just haven't seen any trades."
Moody's Investors Service cut its rating to Ba1 from Baa on Monday. Standard & Poor's Corp cut it's rating of Miami general obligtion debt to single-B from BBB last week.
Both represent non-investment grades, with speculative elements.
Miami has sold 66 bond issues totalling $1.186 billion in the last 30 years, according to Securities Data Corp. Of those, 26 issues totaling $668 million of bonds were insured.
But because a far greater share of the recent debt has been insured, only about $15 million of the outstanding debt is uninsured, traders and those involved in the issues said.
In the secondary market Tuesday, FGIC-insured Miami 5.8s of 2005 were offered at a 4.70 percent net. Kenny Evaluation Services priced the bonds at the close Monday at a 4.78 percent yield.
